 Samsung Stocks Rise for Second Day as Memory Demand Signals Pile Up
 Less than 1 min read 005930 Samsung Electronics (SSNLF) shares rose 1.13% to 196,900 won at the November 19 regular-session close in Seoul, a second straight gain, as afternoon institutional buying lifted the KOSPI's heaviest-weighted component after a weaker open. The KOSPI closed 1.39% higher at 5,137.89, with chipmakers firming ahead of Anthropic's Nasdaq debut. 
 The demand backdrop is getting louder. Nvidia's CFO commentary disclosed that supply commitments rose to $390 billion from $279 billion a quarter earlier, primarily for multiyear memory procurement. Samsung's own third-quarter results showed revenue of 195.3 trillion won and operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, with the chip division contributing 106.5 trillion won. The company scaled up HBM4 sales and expects AI demand in 2027 to far exceed industry supply. 
 Nvidia does not name its suppliers, but a $111 billion jump in commitments tied mainly to memory could support pricing for the largest producers. Annualized, Samsung's third-quarter operating profit is about 430 trillion won against a market value near 1,270 trillion won, roughly 3 times. GuruFocus gives a GF Score of 95/100, with a perfect financial strength rank and high profitability and momentum. Shares sit within 1% of the GF Value of 196,087 won, so the market is pricing a cycle peak, not a bargain. Fourth-quarter HBM4 volumes are the next test.
